overview.text: Ethanol, also called ethyl alcohol or EtOH, is a two-carbon organic alcohol with molecular formula C₂H₆O (structural formula CH₃CH₂OH); its terminal hydroxyl (–OH) group identifies it as an alcohol. It is the intoxicating alcohol in beer, wine, and spirits, but also an important industrial chemical used as a solvent and fuel. Yeast can produce it by fermenting sugars from plant material, while distillation separates it from the fermentation mixture. A notable feature is that ethanol and water form an azeotrope, so ordinary distillation cannot produce completely pure ethanol. Ethanol is also used in some hand sanitizers, though alcohol sanitizers do not eliminate every kind of germ.

key_facts.text: Ethanol’s molecular formula is C₂H₆O; its structural formula, CH₃CH₂OH, shows the hydroxyl group characteristic of alcohols.
Yeast fermentation can produce ethanol from sugars; industrial fuel production may use starch- or sugar-based crops, or cellulosic plant material.
Ethanol is used in beverages, as an industrial and laboratory solvent, and as a fuel.
Because ethanol and water form an azeotrope, ordinary distillation cannot separate them into completely pure ethanol; the source gives a maximum of about 95.6% ethanol by volume.
Some hand sanitizers use ethanol, but alcohol-based sanitizers do not eliminate every kind of germ.
